newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-FIDATOV DOMINATES WORLD CROSS CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FIDATOV DOMINATES WORLD CROSS CHALLENGE.

text.p: Romania's Elena Fidatov continued to dominate the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) World Cross Challenge series by winning the 5.4 km women's race on Saturday.
The 36-year-old Fidatov crossed the line in 17 minutes exactly to record her fourth win of the series.

For most of the race, Fidatov was part of a group of four that included ireland's Catherina McKiernan, South Africa's Colleen De Reuck and Britain's Paula Radcliffe but she moved effortlessly away from her rivals in the final kilometre.
McKiernan, in her first race of the season, was second in 17:08 while De Reuck took third spot in 17:12.
Fidatov continues to lead the overall Cross Challenge rankings, improving her position to 100 points. Ethiopia's Gete Wami, the world champion, did not race but remains second with 88 points.
Kenya's Bernard Barmasai led home three of his compatriots in the 9.7-km men's race after breaking away just beyond the halfway point on the dry but undualting course.
Barmasai was racing for the first time at a European cross country event but showed little inexperience as he won in 27:58.

Ironically, one of the reasons why Barmasai competed here while most of the better known Kenyan runners have returned home is that he did not want to contest the world cross country championships and is concentrating his efforts on the summer track season.
Kenya's Laban Chege was a distant second in 28:14 with compatriot Hezron Mokamba third in 28:19.
The men's Cross Challenge standings are lead by Slovakia's Robert Stefko with 60 points. He finished ninth here but gained enough points to take over at the top from France's Yann Millon.
The Challenge is a 12-race series and has a $25,000 first prize for both the men's and women's winners. The next event is in Albufeira, Portugal, on February 9.
